passage:
“Chetan bhaiya, is it starting?” Sarika ran into the living room in her blue jersey, a flag painted on each cheek.
“Not yet, sit down,” said her brother. “You’ll sit on the good cushion only if you’re quiet.”
“I’m always quiet,” she said loudly. Nani, folding clothes in the corner, laughed but stayed silent. She supported the other team, and everyone knew it.
When the first ball flew for four, Sarika and Chetan jumped up together, shouting and hugging. Sarika’s voice cracked. “We’re going to win, aren’t we?”
Chetan grinned. “Maybe. But we cheer either way.”
Nani smiled and handed Sarika a glass of water.

qa.q: What was painted on Sarika's cheeks?
qa.a: A flag was painted on each of Sarika's cheeks.

qa.q: Why did Sarika's voice crack when she asked whether they would win?
qa.a: Sarika was so excited and so invested in the match that she was almost out of breath, and she wanted reassurance that her side would win.

qa.q: What did Chetan's reply do for Sarika?
qa.a: Chetan said they cheer either way, which took some of the pressure off winning and kept the fun in the moment.

qa.q: How might Nani have felt about the room cheering for a team she did not support?
qa.a: Nani may have felt amused and outnumbered but warm, since she laughed and gave Sarika water. She stayed quiet about her own side.

grounding: Shows a child in team colours cheering with family, feeling instant belonging and being part of a story.

passage:
My name is Ira, and I’m in Class 4. Our whole class loves the same film hero, and on Fridays we all wear his colour. I wear an orange band on my wrist and a scarf. At lunch we do his dance, and even Rohan, who is shy, joins in.
Only Reena wears green because she likes a different hero. She sits at the edge and eats quietly. Yesterday I asked her to show us her favourite song. She looked surprised, then hummed it, and we clapped.
I like being part of something big. It feels like all of us are in the same story, even when the story has two heroes.

qa.q: Which colour does Ira's class wear on Fridays?
qa.a: The class wears the colour of their favourite hero, and Ira wears an orange band and a scarf.

qa.q: How does Ira feel about being part of the class group?
qa.a: Ira feels happy and proud to belong, saying it feels like everyone is in the same story.

qa.q: What small choice did Ira make that changed things for Reena?
qa.a: Ira asked Reena to show the class her favourite song, which gave Reena a way to join in even though Reena likes a different hero.

qa.q: How might Reena feel sitting at the edge while the others do the dance?
qa.a: Reena may feel a little left out, but not sure, since she eats quietly and looked surprised when Ira asked her. Being invited seems to have been welcome.

grounding: Shows a child loving a film hero with a class, wearing the colour together and feeling belonging in a shared story.
